title: Winter Maintenance Routing & Tracking Solution
description:
Under the Highways Act 1980 Leicester City Council is responsible for ensuring the safe passage of vehicles along the highway. This includes gritting the highway network of Leicester during the winter service period when ice and snow can make driving conditions dangerous.\r
\r
We currently have 6 gritting vehicles in our Winter Service fleet. Currently each gritting vehicle is fitted with a tracker and a satellite navigation unit (SatNav) connected to the vehicles Econ Spargo control box. The trackers track each of the vehicle's movement and are used to check the driver's performance. The data from the tracker can be used as evidence in court for any accidents and personal injury claims made against the City Council. The sat nav units have preloaded gritting routes and by having the sat nav system in each vehicle, our drivers can fully concentrate on their driving and not worry about missing out sections due to driver error.\r
\r
The City of Leicester is growing, and the road network is constantly changing. The existing gritting routes on the satnav that were captured by the gritting vehicle trackers and digitised a few years ago are now out of date. These routes need amending and optimising so that the drivers can drive their routes in the safest possible manner, taking the shortest possible distance to minimise fuel usage and delivering the optimum amount of salt over the route.\r
\r
To view the documentation for this opportunity please use the link provided in the Other Information section.

title: Hosting and Maintenance of an Online Web Based Portal for Online Procedures Manuals
description:
Procurement for Hosting and Maintenance of an Online Web Based Portal for Online Procedures Manuals.

The Multi-Agency Safeguarding Arrangements in the geographical area of Leicester, Leicestershire & Rutland (LLR) are the Leicestershire & Rutland Safeguarding Children Partnership and the Leicester Safeguarding Children Partnership Board (SCPs).

The two SCPs collaborate to develop a suite of policies, procedures and protocols to inform (within a multi-agency context) the work of practitioners working across LLR. Therefore, there is an online manual which is accessible to all practitioners, including those from statutory and voluntary agencies.

Each Local Authority (Leicester City Council, Leicestershire County Council, Rutland County Council) has statutory duties set out in the legislation and statutory guidance Working Together 2023 to provide support and protection to vulnerable children.

Each Local Authority requires local single agency procedures, policy and practice guidance which is accessible to the social care workforce in their authority to underpin local practice standards. Whilst this is a separate single agency online procedure manual it must be aligned with and connected to the multi-agency manual provided by the Safeguarding Children Partnership.

The contract period is for 2 years, with the option to extend for up to a maximum of 24 months (in 12-month increments).

title: Regional SEND Mediation Advice, Mediation and Disagreement Resolution Services
description:
On behalf of all Local Authorities in the East Midlands, Lincolnshire County Council is leading the procurement of Regional SEND Mediation Advice Services, Mediation Services and Disagreement Resolution (DR) Services.\r
\r
The East Midlands Region is made up of ten (10) Local Authorities (LAs) as listed below:\r
Derby City Council\r
Derbyshire County Council\r
Leicester City Council\r
Leicestershire County Council\r
Lincolnshire County Council\r
North Northamptonshire Council\r
West Northamptonshire Council\r
Nottingham City Council\r
Nottinghamshire County Council\r
Rutland County Council\r
\r
The Service shall consist of three (3) elements: Mediation Advice Services, Mediation Services and DR Services, and shall be delivered to CYP with SEND aged 0-25 years living within the East Midlands. \r
\r
Lincolnshire County Council will act as the Lead Authority on behalf of all ten (10) LAs within East Midlands for the procurement and contract management of the service: however, the successful Supplier will enter into individual agreements with each LA to deliver the Service.\r
\r
All ten LAs (the Customer) require the supply of unbiased Mediation Advice Services, Mediation Services and DR Services (The Service) for Children and Young People (CYP) with Special Educational Needs and/or Disabilities (SEND) and their families as part of the single route of redress from 1st November 2023. For the avoidance of doubt this means that the Service shall be fully operational from the 1st November 2023.\r
\r
The Children and Families Act (2014) sets out the way in which services and provision are made for families of CYP with SEND aged 0-25 years. This Act, specifically Sections 51-57 and 60, defines the statutory duties for local authorities with regard to appeals, Mediation Advice, Mediation and DR Services, along with Chapter 11 of the associated SEND Code of Practise (COP) 2015. This service shall have due regard to relevant legislation and ensure it supports LAs to meet their statutory duty and the needs of CYP with SEND. \r
\r
Mediation Advice Services and Mediation Services are in place to help settle disputes between CYP, families and LAs relating to Education, Health, and Care (EHC) Needs Assessment requests, EHC Needs Assessments or elements of content within the EHC Plan (EHCP). \r
\r
DR is voluntary for all parties and complements Mediation Advice and Mediation to resolve disagreements which may be related to the fulfilment of duties, SEND provision and health and social care provision for CYP with SEND, including disagreements between health commissioners and LAs.\r
\r
An online supplier briefing event will be held on Monday 26th June 2023 at 10:00am. The online event will briefly outline the requirements of the delivery of Mediation Advice Services, Mediation Services and DR Services in the East Midlands. To book into the briefing event please email fliss.christopher@lincolnshire.gov.uk.

title: ASC0284 - Community Connectors Service
description:
Leicester City Council ('the 'Authority') invited Tenders for the provision of the Community Connectors Service, which will focus on six of the more disadvantaged areas of the city whose residents also report higher levels of social isolation. The Community Connectors (a team of local area co-ordinators) will work within the six selected areas of the city.

The Community Connectors will take a community centred (i.e. Asset Based Community Development based or similar) approach to build confident and connected communities with the aims of reducing isolation and loneliness, improving physical and mental health and reducing health inequalities. The Service will take a holistic approach to addressing isolation and loneliness, ensuring that, in addition to organising social activities and events, people are gently supported and encouraged to make other changes leading to better health and wellbeing and greater social inclusion.

The Authority conducted this procurement under the Light Touch Regime for Social and Other Specific Services, as set out in the Public Contract Regulations 2015 (PCR), at Section 7 (Regulations 74 to 77) and Schedule 3. The procurement process was not conducted under the Public Contract Regulations 2015; however, it was similar to that of an Open procedure. The Process did, unlike an Open Procedure, include the flexibility, as allowed under the Light Touch Regime with various evaluation stages as detailed in the Invitation to Tender documentation.

It was the intention of the Authority to award a block contract to a provider to deliver this service.

The proposed Contract will be for an initial period of 3 years to commence on 9th August 2023 (or before if possible), with an option to extend, subject to satisfactory performance outcomes and agreement by the Authority, for a further period or periods up to a total of 2 years, taking the contract term to a maximum of 5 years.

The Invitation to Tender document and its appendices and all other documentation issued to Tenderers set out the details of the Authority's requirements and how to submit Tenders.

Leicestershire County Council in partnership with Leicester City Council and Rutland County Council (LLR Group) has undertaken this procurement for the provision of Advocacy Services across Leicestershire, Leicester and Rutland.
The successful provider will be responsible for the delivery of four distinct types of advocacy services as listed below:
Independent Mental Capacity Advocacy (IMCA)
The Mental Capacity Act makes statutory provisions for an IMCA to provide independent support for people who lack capacity to make important decisions. This must be provided by an organisation who is independent of the local LLR Group and the NHS.

Independent NHS Complaints Advocacy (ICAS)
This advocacy relates to members of the public or their carers making or intending to make an NHS complaint.

Independent Mental Health Advocacy (IMHA)
This is provided to people who are detained in a secure mental health setting, provisionally discharged, those on Community Treatment Orders and voluntary patients.

Care Act Advocacy
This refers to the statutory requirement under sections 67 and 68 of the Care Act to provide advocacy to people who would experience substantial difficulty in being fully involved in their assessment and other parts of the care pathway

title: PAN3048 - Emergency Repairs Call Handling Service
description:
The Housing Division within Leicester City Council manages just over 19,500 properties and we are the largest landlord in the City. These properties are a mix of houses, bedsits, bungalows, flats, maisonettes and sheltered accommodation.\r
\r
Each year, we complete approximately 130,000 responsive repairs during normal working hours, and those repairs are carried out by around 300 craft operatives.\r
\r
Outside of normal working hours, we provide an emergency repairs service to our tenants, who can report emergency repairs via a published emergency repairs telephone line.\r
\r
Most of these repairs are carried out by our own staff, a small number of whom participate on an emergency repairs rota, but we also use a small number of contractors for more specialist repairs.\r
\r
The services required are the handling of all of the Authority's Housing Divisions emergency repairs calls received on the tenant's emergency repairs telephone number. The Service Provider will be required to identify genuine emergency calls, log an emergency repair job on the Authority's IT system, and issue the job to an Emergency Repair Operative using the Authority's work scheduling system, following the required operational procedures.\r
\r
Average annual call volumes are 18,000 calls received with 9,600 calls requiring an emergency repairs job to be raised and issued to an operative.\r
\r
The proposed Contract will be for three years with an option to extend for a period or periods totalling no more than a further two years. We anticipate awarding to a single Service Provider.

title: FEW1333 - Home Care Services Leicester
description:
The current Home Care Framework (currently named the Domiciliary Support Service) is due to expire on 6th October 2024 with procurement planned for October/November 2023. The contract had the option to extend for up to two years, and these have been utilised. The current jointly commissioned Framework began on 9th October 2017 and is supported by the Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland NHS Integrated Care Board. A commissioning review has been undertaken to re-procure this statutory provision. A multi-disciplinary programme board has overseen the review arrangements which are led by senior officers in the ASC strategic commissioning team. Members include representatives from the Integrated Care Board and NHS Midlands & Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit.

The tender opportunity for the provision of ASC0288 - Home Care Service was advertised on 15th November 2023. The deadline for submissions was 2pm on Tuesday 19th December 2023. In February 2024, due to reasons beyond the Council's control and in line with section 4.22.10 of the ITT (Part One) document, the decision was made to abort the current procurement process ASC0288 - Home Care Service Leicester. A final award will therefore not be made, and the procurement process has been terminated. 

A new procurement exercise for homecare services went live on 26th February 2024. The indicative timeline indicates that contract award won't take place until September/October 2024, which does not leave enough time to mobilise contracts, before the existing contracts expire on 6th October 2024. This is a statutory service, and the waiver is required to bridge the gap between the current contracts ending and the new arrangements being in place after a compliant procurement exercise.

title: ASC0314 - Social Marketing Campaign - Smoking Cessation
description:
Appointment of a full-service social marketing agency to plan and deliver a comprehensive social marketing campaign aimed at increasing the number of smokers attempting to quit in the city.  This will be focussed on areas of the city and groups with the highest smoking rates. The campaign's primary objective is to gather insights into the barriers and facilitators to quitting smoking, encourage access to smoking cessation services, develop tailored marketing collateral, and execute a targeted social media strategy. This initiative aims to increase referrals to the Live Well Leicester Stop Smoking Service and ultimately reduce smoking prevalence in Leicester. 

The procurement process was Targeted Quotation to 3 providers, 2 bids were received of which 1 was compliant.

Contract is for an initial period of 2 years to commence on 1 April 2025, with an option to extend, subject to satisfactory performance outcomes and agreement by the Authority, for further periods up to a total of three (1+1+1) years, taking the contract term to a maximum of 5 years.

noticeIdentifier: Leicester, Leicestershire & Rutland ICB - Appointment Booking
title: Procurement of General Practices Appointment Booking Services for Practices in Leicester, Leicestershire & Rutland ICB
description:
The NHS England National Commercial and Procurement Hub supported NHS Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland ICB to place a new contract for the provision of a General Practice Appointment Booking solution to replace the national contract for appointment booking supplied by Accurx Limited which expired on 30th June 2024. 

NHS Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland ICB's requirement is for an appointment booking solution that enables booking of appointments by patients into GP clinics, long term condition clinics and vaccination clinics with integration with GP clinical systems. The solution is required to meet the digital pathways capabilities that support Modernising General Practice (MGP).

A call-off process from the CCS G-Cloud 13 Framework (RM1557.13) Lot 2: Cloud software was undertaken in accordance with the G-Cloud 13 buyers guide to identify the most suitable provider to deliver requirements. The contract has been awarded to Accurx Limted. 

The contract is awarded for an initial period of 9 months with the option to extend for a further 6 months.
